text: Real-time dashboards — a fabric item built directly on KQL, no power BI involved at all.
Write a query in a KQL queryset, pin it to a dashboard, and it becomes a live tile. This one renders trip counts per minute as a time chart, straight off the raw trip events table.
Every tile can auto-refresh on a timer. Base queries let multiple tiles share filter logic. And cross-filtering lets clicking one tile filter the others — all native to KQL, no semantic model needed.

Real-time dashboards refresh on a simple timer, straight against the eventhouse. Power BI direct lake, from lesson 12, sits behind a semantic model with its own refresh trigger. Both skip a separate copy step — that part's the same.

One's built for operational, seconds-old monitoring. The other's built for business reporting with relationships and measures. Next up: windowing — how you aggregate a stream that never actually ends.
